newsitem.title: JAPAN: Isetan's profits surge, helped by facelift.
newsitem.headline: Isetan's profits surge, helped by facelift.

text.p: Isetan Co, one of Japan's most popular department stores, said on Friday that a facelift at its flagship store helped rake in customers and sent its half-year profits surging by nearly 93 percent.

In the six months to September 30, Isetan said its parent current profit leapt to 2.37 billion yen ($21.3 million) from 1.23 billion yen ($11.0 million) in the same period of the previous year. Revenues grew to 209.70 billion yen ($1.88 billion) from 192.82 billion ($1.73 billion).

"In order to maintain market share amid increasing competition in areas such as Shinjuku, we will try to strengthen our business further," Isetan said in a statement, referring to the location of its main store in Tokyo.

Last month, Japan's oldest department store Takashimaya opened a new shopping mall in central Tokyo, just around the block from Isetan. To compete, Isetan revamped its main store inside and out, introducing new brands and expanding garment size-ranges.

Analysts said that the opening of the Takashimaya "Times Square" shopping complex helped neighbouring large-scale retailers such as Isetan as many new customers visiting the centre also tended to visit its store.

For the business year to March 31, 1997 Isetan forecast a parent current profit of 9.00 billion yen ($81.0 million) against 7.18 billion yen ($64.6 million) the previous year. It said it expected revenues to rise slightly to 440.00 billion yen ($3.96 billion).
Isetan added that it planned to continue its legal battle with Barney's Inc of the United States.

Barney's filed for bankruptcy protection in January and filed suit against Isetan, claiming Isetan is an equity partner in its business. Barney's is trying to recover $50 million in rent payments made to the company.

Isetan denied that it had an equity agreement with the upscale retailer and in return, sued Gene and Bob Pressman, Barney's co-chairmen, to retrieve $168 million in loans that the Pressman brothers personally guaranteed.
The two firms signed an agreement in August under which the bankrupt retailer will keep up "on account" payments to Isetan until March 31, 1997.
